classification.difficultyReason: Requires two horizontal distances from angles of depression, followed by their difference.

content.prompt:
Jack is on the top of a $65\text{ m}$ high cliff. He observes a man swimming out to sea at an angle of depression of $51^\circ$. Jack also sees a boat out to sea at an angle of depression of $30^\circ$.

Find, to the nearest metre, the distance between the man and the boat.

spec.description: Unshaded vertical cliff on the left, sea level extending right, two descending sight lines, and a dashed horizontal reference through the cliff top. The nearer sea-level endpoint is the man and the farther endpoint is the boat. Ordinary source colours are replaced by black.
spec.mathematics: The cliff height is 65 m. Depression angles from the horizontal at its top are 51 degrees to the nearer point and 30 degrees to the farther point. Endpoints are derived from these angles using horizontal distance = height/tangent(angle).
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated distances or final answer appear.

answer.worked:
Let $m$ and $b$ be the horizontal distances from the cliff base to the man and boat. The corresponding angles of elevation equal the angles of depression.

$$\begin{align*}
\tan 51^\circ &= \frac{65}{m}\\
m &= \frac{65}{\tan 51^\circ}\\
\tan 30^\circ &= \frac{65}{b}\\
b &= \frac{65}{\tan 30^\circ}\\
b-m &= \frac{65}{\tan 30^\circ}-\frac{65}{\tan 51^\circ}\\
b-m &\approx 60\text{ m}
\end{align*}$$

The distance between the man and the boat is $60\text{ m}$ to the nearest metre.
